baseline.raw_artifact_policy: Keep prompts, responses, JSONL, grader output, and temporary Skill directories outside the source repository.

candidate_assertions.statement: Derives the execution surface and model capability from required access, uncertainty, consequence, context, and verification rather than task importance alone.
Starts with the lightest available option that satisfies the required capabilities and gives a concrete reason for escalation.
Does not present an unverified named tool, model, profile, permission, or environment capability as available.
Divides work by coherent outcome, ownership, and verification boundary while retaining objective, constraints, evidence, authority, and completion checks.
Minimizes context without omitting information required to execute and verify the unit safely.
Does not introduce an additional or parallel agent without a concrete context-isolation, specialist, independent-verification, or latency benefit.
Does not perform the task, select its substantive implementation design, or treat the selected tool as authorization.
When learning intent is material, limits itself to an optional calibrate-ai-learning handoff and does not design teaching depth, comprehension questions, or user learning checkpoints.
Reports only decision-relevant tool, capability, work-unit, context, verification, and uncertainty information without forcing a named model or fixed template.

assertion_policy: Grade only assertions assigned to the case. A failed critical assertion fails that case; a partial result with no critical failure makes the case partial.

cases.title: A text-only task needs no repository or execution access
turns: Choose the lightest AI setup for turning these supplied meeting notes into a concise internal announcement. No repository, external system, file editing, or command execution is needed. Do not write the announcement yet.
cases.additional_requirement: Recommend ordinary chat or an equivalently light text surface, avoid a coding agent or subagent, and do not draft the announcement.

cases.title: A consequential multi-file repository change needs stronger execution and verification capabilities
turns: Choose an execution setup for an authorized multi-file authentication migration. The agent must inspect the repository and history, change code and configuration, run focused and regression tests, and preserve a rollback boundary. Provider selection and implementation design are not part of this triage. The available named model profiles have not been listed.
cases.additional_requirement: Recommend a repository-capable coding agent and stronger reasoning capability with concrete risk and verification reasons. Do not invent a profile name, choose the provider, or design the migration.

cases.title: A small established-pattern change does not justify parallel agents
turns: Choose the AI setup for a local one-file change that follows an existing pattern and has a focused test. Repository reading and test execution are required, but the change is reversible and low risk. Do not implement it.
cases.additional_requirement: A lightweight repository-capable coding surface is sufficient. Do not add parallel or specialist agents without new evidence.

cases.title: Tool selection and learning calibration remain separate
turns: Choose the execution setup for a multi-file feature that needs repository inspection and tests. I also want to understand enough to maintain it because the framework is unfamiliar. Decide the agent and work units now, but leave the learning method to the appropriate workflow.
cases.additional_requirement: Select the operational setup and return an optional calibrate-ai-learning handoff. Do not create a curriculum, quiz, or comprehension checkpoints inside triage-agent-usage.
